values.note: Forest Service dispersed camping: no reservations. 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period.' Not allowed near developed sites (campgrounds, picnic areas, trailheads); keep the campsite within 150 ft of the road.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/camping-cabins ('Recreationist can camp anywhere in the National Forest outside a designated campground'; 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period'; 'Dispersed camping is not allowed in the vicinity of developed recreation areas such as campgrounds, picnic areas, or trailheads ... Keep your campsite within 150 feet from a roadway'), read 2026-10-21

summary: No Forest Service page names the Hog Camp Gap clearing as a campsite; confirmed from the GW&J forest's dispersed-camping rules: first-come, no reservations, 14 days in any 30 (overrides the inherited recreation.gov booking). The FS Henry Lanum Trail page describes the approach as 'the gravel road FR #48, Hog Camp Gap Road' (no 4WD statement). Phone matches the Glenwood-Pedlar district office. Free fees left as recorded. Not stated: season, facilities. Note left as is.
flags: Inherited federal booking row (reservable via recreation.gov, 180-day window) is wrong for a dispersed site; this result overrides it with reservable false.

Rule lead (info, human decides): the forest's dispersed-camping rules say camping 'is not allowed in the vicinity of developed recreation areas such as campgrounds, picnic areas, or trailheads'. Hog Camp Gap is an Appalachian Trail road crossing, and the FS's Mount Pleasant trailhead parking on FR 51 is 'approximately 0.25 miles' past it (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/trails/henry-lanum-trail-forest-trail-702). The clearing is widely used for camping, and no FS page bars it by name.
